questions.q: Nalanda Mahavihara, the famous centre of Buddhist learning, was founded by which Gupta ruler?
questions.solution: **Kumaragupta I** (5th century CE) founded Nalanda in present-day Bihar. Harsha and the Pala kings later supported it.

questions.q: The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar to commemorate his victory over —
questions.solution: Akbar built the **Buland Darwaza** to commemorate his **conquest of Gujarat** (1573). It is one of the tallest gateways in the world.

questions.q: Along with Annie Besant, which leader started a Home Rule League in 1916?
questions.solution: In 1916 **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** (in April) and **Annie Besant** (in September) set up separate Home Rule Leagues and divided the country between them. Gokhale had died in 1915.
questions.shortcut: Tilak: 'Swaraj is my birthright' → Home Rule.

questions.q: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Cabinet Mission that came to India in 1946?
questions.solution: The **Cabinet Mission (1946)** had three members: **Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander**. **John Simon** led the Simon Commission of 1927-28.

questions.q: Rukmini Devi Arundale, who founded Kalakshetra in Chennai, is associated with which dance form?
questions.solution: **Rukmini Devi Arundale** revived **Bharatanatyam** and founded the Kalakshetra academy (1936) in Chennai.

questions.q: Ustad Zakir Hussain was a world-renowned exponent of which instrument?
questions.solution: **Ustad Zakir Hussain**, son of tabla maestro Ustad Alla Rakha, was the world's best-known **tabla** player.
questions.shortcut: Alla Rakha and Zakir Hussain = tabla father and son.

questions.q: The temples of Khajuraho were built mainly by which dynasty?
questions.solution: The **Chandela** rulers built most of the Khajuraho temples (roughly 950-1050 CE) in present-day Madhya Pradesh. They are known for the Nagara style of architecture.
questions.shortcut: Khajuraho (Bundelkhand, MP) → Chandelas; Cholas are the far south.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission?
questions.solution: **Article 324** gives the Election Commission control of elections to Parliament, the state legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President. Article 280 covers the Finance Commission, 315 the Public Service Commissions, and 368 amendments.

questions.q: A joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament is presided over by the —
questions.solution: Under Article 108 the President *summons* a joint sitting, but the **Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides** over it (Article 118(4)). If the Speaker is absent, the Deputy Speaker presides.

questions.q: The Right to Education (Article 21A) was inserted into the Constitution by which Amendment Act?
questions.solution: The **86th Amendment Act, 2002** inserted **Article 21A** (free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14). It also added a related Fundamental Duty (Article 51A(k)) and changed Article 45.

questions.q: Which writ is issued to produce a detained person before a court to examine whether the detention is lawful?
questions.solution: **Habeas corpus** ('you may have the body') orders the authority holding a person to bring that person before the court. Mandamus commands a public official to do a duty; certiorari and prohibition are issued to lower courts.

questions.q: The Satpura Range lies between which two rivers?
questions.solution: The **Satpura Range** runs between the **Narmada** (to the north) and the **Tapi** (to the south). Both rivers flow west through rift valleys into the Arabian Sea.
questions.shortcut: Vindhya – Narmada – Satpura – Tapi, from north to south.

questions.q: Which state is the largest producer of tea in India?
questions.solution: **Assam** produces more tea than any other Indian state; the Brahmaputra valley is the heart of Indian tea. West Bengal (Darjeeling and the Dooars) comes second.

questions.q: The Kalahari Desert is located mainly in which country?
questions.solution: The **Kalahari**, a semi-arid sandy desert in southern Africa, covers most of **Botswana**. The Atacama is in Chile and the Gobi is in Mongolia.

questions.q: India's First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) was based on which economic model?
questions.solution: The **First Plan** followed the **Harrod-Domar model**, focusing on agriculture and irrigation. The Second Plan used the Mahalanobis model for heavy industry.

questions.q: Which of the following is a direct tax?
questions.solution: A **direct tax** is paid by the same person on whom it is levied — **income tax** is the standard example. GST, customs and excise are indirect taxes whose burden passes on to the consumer.
questions.shortcut: Burden can't be shifted = direct (income, corporate tax).

questions.q: Hypermetropia (long-sightedness) is corrected using which type of lens?
questions.solution: In **hypermetropia**, the image of a nearby object forms behind the retina. A **convex (converging) lens** brings it forward onto the retina.

questions.q: To hear a distinct echo, the reflected sound must reach the ear at least how long after the original sound?
questions.solution: The ear keeps a sound for about **0.1 s** (persistence of hearing). So an echo is distinct only if it returns after at least 0.1 s. With sound at about 344 m/s, the reflecting surface must be at least **about 17 m** away.

questions.q: Rusting of iron requires the presence of —
questions.solution: Iron rusts (forms hydrated iron(III) oxide) only when **both oxygen and water** are present. This is why painting, oiling and galvanising, which keep out air and moisture, prevent rusting.

questions.q: Vinegar is a dilute solution of which acid?
questions.solution: Vinegar is about 5-8% **acetic (ethanoic) acid**. Citric acid is found in citrus fruits, lactic acid in curd, and oxalic acid in spinach and tomatoes.
questions.shortcut: Vinegar = acetic; curd = lactic; lemon = citric.

questions.q: Which metal is present at the centre of the chlorophyll molecule?
questions.solution: The chlorophyll molecule has a **magnesium** ion at its centre. Iron plays the matching role in haemoglobin.

questions.q: Which part of the human brain controls involuntary actions such as breathing and heartbeat?
questions.solution: The **medulla oblongata** in the hindbrain controls involuntary vital functions such as breathing, heartbeat and blood pressure. The cerebrum handles thinking and voluntary action.

questions.q: Who wrote the novel 'Anandamath', which contains the song 'Vande Mataram'?
questions.solution: **Bankim Chandra Chatterjee** wrote **Anandamath** (1882), which includes 'Vande Mataram', India's National Song. Tagore wrote the National Anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana'.
questions.shortcut: National Song = Bankim; National Anthem = Tagore.

questions.q: The Davis Cup is associated with which sport?
questions.solution: The **Davis Cup** is the international men's team competition in **tennis**. Badminton's men's team event is the Thomas Cup, and golf has the Ryder Cup.
questions.shortcut: Davis = tennis; Thomas = badminton; Ryder = golf.

questions.q: In August 2026, it was announced that ISRO will stop building launch vehicles so that this work moves to —
questions.solution: On 21 August 2026, IN-SPACe chairman **Pawan Goenka** announced that **ISRO will hand launch-vehicle building to the Indian private sector**, with ISRO focusing on deep-space and advanced R&D.
questions.shortcut: Aug 2026 = 'privatise the hard tech' month: ISRO vehicles out, DRDO missile tech shared with industry.
